minutes.headline: Board split 2-2 on reading the town manager's evaluation aloud; review will be discussed and finalized next week.
minutes.summary: The Select Board spent most of the meeting on the town manager's annual evaluation. Two members objected to discussing a 22-page composite they had just received; a motion to table failed on a tie and the chair read the whole document into the record. The board also approved a toll booth, a road closure, three committee appointments and an entertainment license with conditions, heard a skate park update and the town manager's report, and discussed the missing ballot questions at Town Meeting before going into executive session.

public_comment.topic: Thanked a departing board member for six years of service and gave the town manager a vote of confidence ahead of her evaluation; Memorial Day ceremony on May 27.
Asked for more citizen participation in drafting the special events policy and raised stormwater runoff on Holman Street into Mullis Brook.
Police chief shared a log of a typical workday to show the demands on department heads; the former town manager's thanks relayed.
Commended the evaluation process and called for a full report on why the ballot questions did not reach the ballot.

votes.motion: Approve the Boys and Girls Club toll booth request for Saturday May 18, 9 to 2, at the center intersection.
Approve the road closure for the cruise night with a rain date of June 19.
Appoint Ken Jones as Conservation Commission representative to the land acquisition committee.
Appoint Karen Menard to the Housing Authority as governor's appointee, term to expire May 1, 2021.
Appoint Greg Burns to the Agricultural Commission, term expiring June 30, 2022.

Approve the weekday and Sunday entertainment license for Fantasia family getaway at 138 Howard Street, Aug 2-4, with a cap of 200 tickets, noise hours as proposed and department head concerns met; amended to no more than eight hours of amplified music per day.
Table the town manager evaluation discussion to next week.
Read the evaluation into the record tonight and hold the discussion next week.
Endorse the composite performance review (withdrawn without a vote).
Enter executive session to conduct strategy for negotiations with non-union personnel (town manager), not to return to public session.

what_happened.line: The Select Board split 2-2 on tabling the town manager's evaluation, then 2-2 on reading it tonight and discussing it next week; both motions failed.
The chair read the full composite evaluation into the record, and the board agreed to seek a consensus next week, with edits going to the chair meanwhile.
The board approved a toll booth, a cruise night road closure and an appointment to the Agricultural Commission; two other appointment votes were not audible.
The board approved an entertainment license for a three-day family event, amended to cap amplified music at eight hours a day.
The quarterly financial report was held over to next week and is to go first on the agenda; the missing ballot questions were left to the new board.

why_it_matters: The town manager's evaluation is the board's main review of who runs town departments, and its final form will not be set until the board meets again.
Ballot questions that did not reach the Town Meeting ballot will not be addressed until after the election, so voters should not expect them on this cycle's ballot.
The quarterly financial report, which shows how the current budget is tracking, was delayed by a week.
watch_next: Next week's Select Board meeting: discussion and consensus on the composite evaluation, and the quarterly financial report first on the agenda.
Whether the board endorses the town manager's recycling contamination grant application.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on most votes, including both 2-2 failures, and on most figures such as $42,000, $130,000 and the grant amounts. The main differences are that ours could not hear the outcomes of the Ken Jones and Menard appointments, that ours records the Greg Burns appointment and a withdrawn endorsement motion that the official minutes lack, and that ours lists only three board members where the official lists four.
